decisions.rationale: Intended Mega: Gengar-Mega. Lead Gengar+Aegislash — both Ghost-types are immune to Sneasler's Fake Out and Close Combat; Aegislash is immune to Dire Claw too (Poison vs Steel 0x), so Sneasler literally cannot damage it. Gengar-Mega (200 Spe) outspeeds all, traps with Shadow Tag, breaks Sneasler sash with 4x SE Psychic for turn-2 KO. Aegislash walls Kleavor (all moves NVE/immune). Back: Serperior (181 Spe) OHKOs Blastoise-Mega and Hippowdon with Leaf Storm, snowballs via Contrary; Gyarados provid
decisions.notebook:
Opponent roster: Sneasler (FocusSash/Unburden, Jolly, 154-189 Spe), Whimsicott (MentalHerb/Prankster, Timid, 149-184), Blastoise-Mega (Blastoisinite/MegaLauncher, Modest, 98-130), Hippowdon (Sitrus/SandStream, Impish, 67-99), Kleavor (ChoiceScarf/Sharpness, Jolly, 115-150 → 172-225 with scarf), Clefable (Leftovers/MagicGuard, Bold, 80-112).

Key structural facts:
- Gengar+Aegislash both Ghost: immune to Fake Out (Normal), Close Combat (Fighting). Aegislash also immune to Dire Claw (Poison vs Steel 0x). Sneasler has ZERO damaging moves vs Aegislash.
- Gengar-Mega 200 Spe outspeeds entire opponent roster. Shadow Tag traps (no switching).
- Gengar Psychic is 4x SE vs Sneasler (92.5-211.6% — breaks sash, possible OHKO without sash).
- Blastoise-Mega Dark Pulse = 80 BP × 1.5 Mega Launcher = 120 BP eff, 2x SE vs Gengar. Major OHKO threat to Gengar-Mega. Serperior is the answer (Leaf Storm 2x SE vs Water).
- Aegislash is 2x WEAK to Earthquake (Ground vs Steel 2x). Not immune! Switch to Gyarados (Flying immune) or Serperior (Grass resists 0.5x) vs Hippowdon.
- Kleavor walled by Aegislash: StoneAxe 0.5x, XScissor 0.25x, CloseCombat immune, Uturn 0.25x.
- Whimsicott Encore threat on Aegislash — avoid repeated King's Shield.

Plan: Lead Gengar+Aegislash, trap+KO Sneasler by turn 2, then bring Serperior for Blastoise/Hippowdon and Gyarados for Intimidate+physical pressure. Watch for Tailwind making opponent faster than Serperior (181).

decisions.rationale: Intended Mega: Blastoise. Lead pair Sneasler and Whimsicott execute turn-one Fake Out disruption and Prankster Tailwind to seize absolute speed control against fast threats like Serperior and Gengar. Backline Blastoise and Hippowdon complete the plan by leveraging Mega Launcher special coverage and Sand Stream passive pressure.
decisions.notebook: Bring Sneasler, Whimsicott, Mega Blastoise, and Hippowdon against Ghostly Labyrinth Masters threat core. Whimsicott sets Tailwind and controls board with Encore against support. Blastoise melts Aegislash and Gengar. Hippowdon provides sand chip and Earthquake.

decisions.rationale: Mega Evolve Gengar for Shadow Tag, trapping Sneasler (can't switch). Psychic 4x SE breaks Focus Sash (92.5-211.6%), leaving Sneasler at 1 HP for easy KO next turn. Aegislash Flash Cannon chips Whimsicott 40.7-93.3%. Sneasler cannot damage either Ghost type. Even if Sneasler Protects, Shadow Tag is active and Whimsicott takes chip damage. Tailwind likely goes up via Prankster but Sneasler still can't threaten our Ghost core.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 lead: Gengar+Aegislash vs Sneasler+Whimsicott. Plan: Mega Gengar T1 for Shadow Tag, break Sneasler sash with Psychic, KO T2. Aegislash chips Whimsicott with Flash Cannon. Tailwind from Prankster Whimsicott likely T1 — expect opponent speed doubling for 4 turns. Sneasler Unburden triggers when sash pops (154-189→308-378 Spe). Sneasler has zero meaningful damage vs Ghost/Steel-Ghost core. After Sneasler KO, bring Serperior for Blastoise-Mega (Leaf Storm 2x SE) and Gyarados for Hippowdon EQ immunity + Intimidate. Watch Encore from Whimsicott on Aegislash — avoid repeated King's Shield. Blastoise-Mega Dark Pulse (120 BP eff via Mega Launcher) is major threat to Gengar-Mega; Serperior is the switch-in answer.

decisions.rationale: Sneasler's Fake Out halts Gengar's potential Mega evolution/attack threat for Turn 1, while Whimsicott safely sets up Tailwind. Both opposing Pokémon (Gengar and Aegislash) are immune to Fighting/Poison and Normal (Fake Out hits Gengar if un-Mega'd, though Gengar's item is Gengarite; wait, Fake Out hits Gengar before Mega, but Gengar is Ghost-type so Fake Out doesn't hit Gengar anyway!). Let's check: Gengar is Ghost/Poison. Normal-type Fake Out is immune against Ghost! Wait, Sneasler's options:
decisions.notebook: Sneasler and Whimsicott lead against Gengar and Aegislash. Ghost-types are immune to Sneasler's Fake Out and Close Combat/Dire Claw. Tailwind is critical on turn 1 to outspeed and pressure with Blastoise and Hippowdon in the back.

decisions.rationale: Sneasler is at 1% HP with Unburden active and Tailwind up, but Gengar is immune to Sneasler's attacks and can KO Sneasler through priority or speed if Sneasler doesn't protect. Bringing in Blastoise safely behind Sneasler's Protect lets Blastoise apply pressure on turn 2.
decisions.notebook: Sneasler and Whimsicott lead against Gengar and Aegislash. Ghost-types are immune to Sneasler's Fighting and Normal/Poison attacks. Tailwind is critical on turn 1 to outspeed and pressure with Blastoise and Hippowdon in the back.

decisions.rationale: Shadow Ball chips Blastoise (34-62%) while King's Shield protects Aegislash-Blade from Mega Dark Pulse and reverts to Shield forme (150/150). Sneasler at 1% is trapped by Shadow Tag and cannot damage either Ghost type—keeping it alive as a dead slot is better than KOing it and letting opponent bring in Hippowdon/Kleavor/Clefable. Gengar survives Dark Pulse (~36-54% with Mega Launcher). Next turn KO Sneasler and continue pressuring Blastoise with Aegislash in safe Shield forme.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag trapping all opponent non-Ghost mons. Sneasler sash consumed, Unburden active, at 1%—useless dead slot, keep alive to deny opponent a useful switch-in. Blastoise likely Mega Evolves T2; Mega Launcher boosts Dark Pulse to ~120 BP (tool omits abilities, multiply ~1.5x). Aegislash in Blade forme after T1 Flash Cannon—King's Shield reverts to Shield (150/150). Opponent Tailwind 3 turns left. Plan: chip Blastoise T2, KO Sneasler T3, then bring Serperior for Blastoise-Mega (Leaf Storm 2x SE) and Gyarados for Hippowdon EQ immunity. Watch for Encore from fainted Whimsicott—no longer a threat. Kleavor Choice Scarf 115-150 raw speed, outspeeds unboosted Gengar-Mega (200) only under Tailwind.

decisions.rationale: Serperior is the only remaining Pokémon that can KO Blastoise-Mega at 59% this turn cycle (Leaf Storm 2x SE + Expert Belt, range ~42-121% raw). Gyarados can't threaten Blastoise and is weak to Kleavor's Stone Axe. Aegislash survives one Dark Pulse in Shield forme (~60-85% w/ Mega Launcher), buying Serperior a window to fire Leaf Storm next turn. King's Shield can also block Dark Pulse if predicted.
decisions.notebook:
Opponent roster G1: Sneasler (Jolly, Focus Sash/Unburden, Fake Out/CC/Dire Claw/Protect), Whimsicott (Timid, Mental Herb/Prankster—fainted), Blastoise-Mega (Modest, Mega Launcher, Water Pulse/Aura Sphere/Dark Pulse/Protect), Hippowdon (Impish, Sitrus/Sand Stream, EQ/Rock Slide/Slack Off/Protect), Kleavor (Jolly, Choice Scarf/Sharpness, Stone Axe/X-Scissor/CC/U-turn), Clefable (Bold, Leftovers/Magic Guard, Moonblast/Follow Me/Protect/Moonlight).
Key calcs: Blastoise-Mega Dark Pulse w/ Mega Launcher (~120 BP) does ~60-85% to Aegislash Shield forme (167 HP). Serperior Leaf Storm (130 BP, 2x SE, Expert Belt ~1.2x) likely KOs Blastoise at 59%. Kleavor Scarf+Tailwind outspeeds entire team.
Plan: Serperior KOs Blastoise with Leaf Storm, then snowballs with Contrary on Hippowdon (2x SE). Gyarados saved for Ground immunity vs Hippowdon EQ and late-game DD sweep. Aegislash uses King's Shield to stay in Shield forme and block Dark Pulse if Blastoise targets it. Watch for opponent switching Sneasler (1%) to Hippowdon/Kleavor now that Shadow Tag is gone.

decisions.rationale: Sneasler is at 1% and must Protect to avoid being picked off. Mega Blastoise outspeeds both under Tailwind and hits both for super-effective damage with Dark Pulse (Mega Launcher boosted). Gengar is fast and fragile, while Aegislash threatens heavy damage if left unchecked.
decisions.notebook: Sneasler can use Unburden speed under Tailwind. Blastoise-Mega deals massive super-effective Dark Pulse damage.

decisions.rationale: Sneasler outspeeds all and can OHKO Serperior with Dire Claw (79-113%), so Protect is mandatory. King's Shield has ~33% success rate (used once), making it unreliable. Sacred Sword KOs Sneasler at 1% and hits switch-ins hard (SE Kleavor, neutral Hippowdon from high Blade Atk). Aegislash's SpDef is identical in both formes, so Dark Pulse (40-56%) is survivable. Next turn King's Shield returns to Shield forme; Serperior Leaf Storms Blastoise.
decisions.notebook:
Opponent roster G1: Sneasler (Jolly, Focus Sash/Unburden, Fake Out/CC/Dire Claw/Protect), Whimsicott (Timid, Mental Herb/Prankster—fainted), Blastoise-Mega (Modest, Mega Launcher, Water Pulse/Aura Sphere/Dark Pulse/Protect), Hippowdon (Impish, Sitrus/Sand Stream, EQ/Rock Slide/Slack Off/Protect), Kleavor (Jolly, Choice Scarf/Sharpness, Stone Axe/X-Scissor/CC/U-turn), Clefable (Bold, Leftovers/Magic Guard, Moonblast/Follow Me/Protect/Moonlight).
Key calcs: Sneasler Dire Claw 79-113% vs Serperior (possible OHKO). Blastoise Dark Pulse 40-56% vs Aegislash Shield (SpDef same in both formes). Serperior Leaf Storm 55-121% vs Blastoise at 59% (possible KO). Kleavor Scarf+Tailwind outspeeds entire team.
Plan: Protect Serperior from Dire Claw this turn, KO Sneasler with Aegislash Sacred Sword. Next turn: King's Shield Aegislash back to Shield forme, Serperior Leaf Storm KOs Blastoise (+2 SpA from Contrary). Gyarados saved for Ground immunity vs Hippowdon EQ and late-game DD sweep. Watch for opponent sacking Sneasler to bring Hippowdon (Sand Stream) or Kleavor (Scarf). If Hippowdon comes in, switch Aegislash to Gyarados for EQ immunity + Intimidate.

decisions.rationale: Sneasler outspeeds Serperior under Tailwind and can hit it super-effectively with Dire Claw (with a chance to KO or status), while Blastoise-Mega targets Serperior with Dark Pulse. Aegislash is immune to Fighting and Poison.
decisions.notebook: Sneasler Unburden Speed outspeeds under Tailwind. Blastoise-Mega Mega Launcher boosts pulse moves.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Leaf Storm->Hippowdon for possible OHKO (64-147%) and guaranteed +2 SpA from Contrary. Hippowdon unlikely to Protect (just switched in, wants to use last Tailwind turn). King's Shield (priority +4) safely reverts Aegislash to Shield forme, blocking EQ/Dark Pulse. Next turn without Tailwind, Serperior at 181 outspeeds both foes and +2 Leaf Storm KOs Blastoise. Targeting Blastoise risks wasting move if it Protects at 59%.
decisions.notebook: Opponent roster G1: Sneasler (Jolly, Focus Sash/Unburden, Fake Out/CC/Dire Claw/Protect), Whimsicott (Timid, Mental Herb/Prankster—fainted), Blastoise-Mega (Modest, Mega Launcher, Water Pulse/Aura Sphere/Dark Pulse/Protect), Hippowdon (Impish, Sitrus/Sand Stream, EQ/Rock Slide/Slack Off/Protect), Kleavor (Jolly, Choice Scarf/Sharpness, Stone Axe/X-Scissor/CC/U-turn), Clefable (Bold, Leftovers/Magic Guard, Moonblast/Follow Me/Protect/Moonlight). Key calcs: Serperior Leaf Storm 64-147% vs full HP Hippowdon (possible OHKO). Leaf Storm 55-121% vs Blastoise. Blastoise Dark Pulse 37-64% vs Serperior. Rock Slide 22-39% vs Serperior (spread). Dark Pulse 40-56% vs Aegislash Shield. Kleavor Scarf+Tailwind outspeeds entire team. Plan: After this turn (Tailwind expires), Serperior at 181 outspeeds both remaining foes. With +2 SpA from Contrary, +2 Leaf Storm KOs Blastoise. Gyarados saved for Ground immunity vs Hippowdon EQ and late-game DD sweep. Switch Aegislash to Gyarados next turn if Hippowdon survives and threatens EQ. Endgame: Serperior + Gyarados clean up.

decisions.rationale: Tailwind expires this turn, and Blastoise outspeeds Serperior while it lasts. Aegislash-Blade takes super-effective damage from Dark Pulse, so targeting Aegislash-Blade with Dark Pulse and spreading with Rock Slide pressures both threats effectively while avoiding Hippowdon hitting Blastoise with Earthquake.

Serperior outspeeds (181 vs 98-130) and +2 Leaf Storm is guaranteed KO on Blastoise at 53% (60-106% base, ×2.25 from +2 SpA). Shadow Ball from Aegislash as backup chip if Leaf Storm misses (10%). If Blastoise Protects, we repeat next turn with same guaranteed KO. This is game-winning.
decisions.notebook: Opponent roster G1: Sneasler (Jolly, Focus Sash/Unburden, Fake Out/CC/Dire Claw/Protect), Whimsicott (Timid, Mental Herb/Prankster—fainted), Blastoise-Mega (Modest, Mega Launcher, Water Pulse/Aura Sphere/Dark Pulse/Protect), Hippowdon (Impish, Sitrus/Sand Stream, EQ/Rock Slide/Slack Off/Protect), Kleavor (Jolly, Choice Scarf/Sharpness, Stone Axe/X-Scissor/CC/U-turn), Clefable (Bold, Leftovers/Magic Guard, Moonblast/Follow Me/Protect/Moonlight). Key calcs: Serperior Leaf Storm 60-106% vs full HP Blastoise (without boosts); with +2 SpA guaranteed KO. Blastoise Dark Pulse 40-56% vs Aegislash Shield. Kleavor Scarf+Tailwind outspeeds entire team. Gyarados saved for Ground immunity vs Hippowdon EQ and late-game DD sweep. Serperior +2 SpA from Contrary makes Leaf Storm guaranteed KO on Blastoise-Mega at 53%.

decisions.rationale: Serperior is at +2 SpA and resists Water, while Aegislash is immune to Aura Sphere and resisted by nothing from Blastoise except Dark Pulse (2x SE). Dark Pulse into Aegislash pressures the Ghost/Steel type while it might King's Shield or attack. Protect is risky if Serperior double-targets or uses Leaf Storm freely, but Dark Pulse into Aegislash is our best neutral/super-effective breaker.
decisions.notebook: Blastoise-Mega Mega Launcher boosts pulse moves. Aegislash uses King's Shield and Ghost/Steel attacks.

decisions.rationale: Dragon Pulse is 100% accuracy and guaranteed KO on Blastoise at 10% with +2 SpA — strictly safer than Leaf Storm's 90%. Serperior outspeeds so it lands first. Aegislash King's Shield covers the only threat: Blastoise Protects this turn, then we repeat next turn with Aegislash safely in Shield forme. If Blastoise doesn't Protect, Serperior KOs and the game ends.
decisions.notebook: Opponent roster G1: Sneasler (Jolly, Focus Sash/Unburden, Fake Out/CC/Dire Claw/Protect), Whimsicott (Timid, Mental Herb/Prankster—fainted), Blastoise-Mega (Modest, Mega Launcher, Water Pulse/Aura Sphere/Dark Pulse/Protect), Hippowdon (Impish, Sitrus/Sand Stream, EQ/Rock Slide/Slack Off/Protect), Kleavor (Jolly, Choice Scarf/Sharpness, Stone Axe/X-Scissor/CC/U-turn), Clefable (Bold, Leftovers/Magic Guard, Moonblast/Follow Me/Protect/Moonlight). Key calcs: Serperior +2 SpA Dragon Pulse guaranteed KO on Blastoise-Mega at 10% (100% acc, 11.8-26.6%). Blastoise Dark Pulse guaranteed KO on Aegislash Blade at 33% (71.9-125.7%). Kleavor Scarf+Tailwind outspeeds entire team. Gyarados saved for Ground immunity vs Hippowdon EQ and late-game DD sweep. Opponent tends to Protect-stall when cornered.

decisions.rationale: Blastoise-Mega is slower than Serperior and must survive a possible attack, but Aegislash-Blade is weak to Dark Pulse (boosted by Mega Launcher). Since Aegislash is at 32%, Dark Pulse into Aegislash-Blade is our best path to KO it and leave a 1v1 against Serperior. Hippowdon is fainted so it passes.
decisions.notebook: Blastoise-Mega utilizes Mega Launcher-boosted Dark Pulse to pressure Aegislash-Blade.

reflections.summary: Won because Serperior's Contrary Leaf Storm snowballed to +4 SpA, OHKOing Hippowdon and finishing Blastoise-Mega, while Aegislash's King's Shield stalling absorbed Dark Pulse pressure. Gengar-Mega traded itself for ~40% on Blastoise before dying to Dark Pulse — a net loss, but Serperior cleaned up the weakened opponent easily.
reflections.adjustment: Gengar-Mega was a liability vs Blastoise-Mega (outspeeds and OHKOs with Dark Pulse). Next game consider leading Gyarados instead for Intimidate on Sneasler and Ground immunity, saving Gengar-Mega for a matchup where Shadow Tag actually traps something. Opponent will likely adapt to Serperior — expect Kleavor (Scarf) and/or Clefable brought to handle it.
reflections.notebook: Opponent G1 brought: Sneasler, Whimsicott, Blastoise-Mega, Hippowdon. Benched: Kleavor (Scarf), Clefable. Blastoise-Mega spams Dark Pulse repeatedly — outspeeds and OHKOs Gengar-Mega. Whimsicott Tailwind never resolved (lost move turn 4). Opponent Protect-stalls when cornered (confirmed). Serperior +2 Leaf Storm OHKOs Hippowdon; +4 Dragon Pulse KOs Blastoise-Mega. Aegislash Sacred Sword fails to OHKO Sash Sneasler but KOs after Sash consumed. Gyarados never needed G1 — keep available for Ground immunity and late DD. Next game expect opponent to bring Kleavor + Clefable to counter Serperior; plan Intimidate/redirect answers. Gengar-Mega poor into Blastoise-Mega lead; reconsider Mega slot if Blastoise-Mega confirmed.

reflections.summary: Lost because the initial matchup plan brought Whimsicott and Sneasler, whose supportive and physical offensive profiles struggled against the opponent's defensive backbone of Aegislash and Contrary Serperior once Mega Gengar was removed, leaving Mega Blastoise and Hippowdon isolated against setup and King's Shield stalling.
reflections.adjustment: For Game 2, bring special-oriented or direct-spreading threats that bypass King's Shield and can break Serperior and Aegislash without relying on vulnerable physical setup or Tailwind support.
reflections.notebook: Blastoise-Mega utilizes Mega Launcher-boosted Dark Pulse to pressure Aegislash-Blade. Opponent's team includes Serperior (Expert Belt, Contrary, Leaf Storm/Dragon Pulse/Protect), Aegislash (Leftovers, King's Shield, Sacred Sword, Shadow Ball, Flash Cannon), Mega Gengar, and Gyarados.
